You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this - finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool - does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only - your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

Initialize a StGit stack on a branch.

Initializing a branch with a StGit stack commits initial, empty stack state for the
branch to the repository. Theses stack metadata commits are tracked by the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` reference. Updated stack state is committed by each StGit command
that modifies the stack. StGit users do not have to do anything with the
`refs/stacks/<branch>` ref directly.

Some StGit commands, such as `stg new` and `stg uncommit`, will automatically initialize
the stack, so it is often not necessary to explicitly initialize the stack on a branch.
Also, branches created with `stg branch --create` are automatically initialized.

The branch must already exist and point to a commit before initializing a StGit stack.

StGit stack metadata can be deinitialized from a branch using `stg branch --cleanup`.

payload.output:
Show all the patches in the series, or just those in the given range, ordered from
bottom to top.

The topmost applied patch is prefixed with '>'. All other applied patches are prefixed
with '+'. Unapplied patches are prefixed with '-' and hidden patches with '!'.

The --reverse option may be used to reverse the order in which patches are displayed.
The reversed order is more stack-like, with the base of the stack appearing at the
bottom of of the display.

Empty patches are prefixed with a '*' when the --empty option is used.

Usage: stg series [OPTIONS] [-A] [-U] [-H]
       stg series [OPTIONS] --all
       stg series [OPTIONS] --short
       stg series [OPTIONS] [patch]...

Arguments:
  [patch]...
          Patches to display

Options:
  -b, --branch <branch>
          Use <branch> instead of current branch

      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Select Options:
  -a, --all
          Select all patches, including hidden patches

  -s, --short[=<n>]
          Select <n> patches around the topmost patch only

  -A, --applied
          Select the applied patches only

  -U, --unapplied
          Select the unapplied patches only

  -H, --hidden
          Select the hidden patches only

  -m, --missing <branch>
          Select patches in <branch> not present in current branch

Display Options:
      --author
          Display author name for each patch

  -c, --count
          Display the number of selected patches and exit

  -i, --commit-id[=<length>]
          Display the commit id for each patch.
          
          The optional length indicates how many prefix characters of the commit id to
          display. The default is "full", which displays the full commit id, but may
          alternatively be specified as a positive integer greater than or equal to 4.

  -d, --description
          Display short description for each patch

  -e, --empty
          Before the '+', '>', '-', and '!' prefixes, print a column that contains
          either '0' (for empty patches) or a space (for non-empty patches).

Show the history of changes to the stack. If one or more patch names are given, only the
changes affecting those patches are shown.

The 'stg undo' and 'stg redo' commands may be used to step back and forth through
historical stack states. The 'stg reset' command may be used to reset the stack directly
to a historic state.

The '--clear' option may be used to delete the stack's change history. Undo and redo are
unavailable on a stack without change history. Clearing the stack state history cannot
be undone.

Usage: stg log [OPTIONS] [--] [patch]...
       stg log --clear

Arguments:
  [patch]...
          Only show history for these patches

Options:
  -b, --branch <branch>
          Use <branch> instead of current branch

  -d, --diff
          Show stack state diffs

  -n, --number <n>
          Limit output to <n> commits

  -f, --full
          Show using full commit log format

  -g, --graphical
          Run gitk instead of printing to stdout

      --clear
          Clear the stack history

      --color <when>

args.prompt_template:
You are helping reimplement the StGit 2.5.5 CLI tool (`stg`) from scratch by observing the behavior of a reference binary at `/workspace/executable`. This is a clean-room reverse-engineering benchmark.

STRICT RULES:
- You may ONLY run `/workspace/executable` with various flags/args and inspect the git repositories it creates. NEVER run objdump/readelf/nm/strings/strace/ltrace/gdb or any binary analysis on it. NEVER search the internet or package registries for StGit source code. Behavioral observation only.
- Do all experiments in throwaway git repos under /tmp, e.g. `mkdir /tmp/exp_$$_NAME && cd ... && git init -q && git commit -q --allow-empty -m initial`. git is already configured with user.name/user.email.
- Run git with `git config --global --add safe.directory '*'` first if you hit "dubious ownership".

Background you can rely on (already discovered):
- Stack state lives in ref `refs/stacks/<branch>`, whose tree contains `stack.json` (JSON, 2-space indent, no trailing newline; keys: version=5, prev, head, applied[], unapplied[], hidden[], patches{name:{oid}}) and `patches/<name>` metadata blobs.
- Commands print transaction output like `+ p1` (applied), `> p2` (topmost), `- p3` (unapplied), ranges like `- p4..p5`.
- Errors print `error: <msg>` to stderr, exit code 2 typically.

YOUR ASSIGNED EXPLORATION TASK:
{{item}}

METHODOLOGY:
- Exercise every flag and positional-argument combination of the assigned commands. Try edge cases: empty stack, no patches applied, all patches popped, nonexistent patch names, ambiguous/duplicate names, invalid input, conflicts (e.g. push with a conflicting worktree), dirty worktree vs clean worktree, operating from a subdirectory, detached HEAD, `-b/--branch` on another branch.
- Record EXACT stdout and stderr (quote them verbatim, including trailing punctuation and blank lines) and the exit code for each case. Note which stream each line goes to (use `1>/tmp/out 2>/tmp/err` to separate when it matters).
- Note side effects: contents of stack.json afterwards, branch HEAD changes, refs created.
- For output that involves colors, re-run with `--color always` and record the raw escape sequences (e.g. via `od -c` or `cat -v`).

DELIVERABLE:
- Write a thorough, well-organized spec to `/workspace/observed/<group>.md` (create the dir; <group> = a short name for your assigned group). Include exact command lines you ran and their exact outputs/exit codes. This file is the primary deliverable — make it complete enough that someone can implement the commands without rerunning the binary.
- Your final reply to me: a compact summary (10-30 lines) of the most important/surprising findings. Do not paste the whole file.
items: GROUP=help. Dump the complete --help AND -h (short help) output of EVERY stg subcommand into individual files under /workspace/observed/help/ (e.g. new.help.txt, new.h.txt). Commands: diff files id log name show edit fold new refresh rename spill sync email export next patches prev series top branch clean commit delete float goto hide import init pick pop pull push rebase redo repair reset sink squash uncommit undo unhide completion version help. Also capture: `stg --help`, `stg -h`, `stg help`, `stg help <cmd>` for a few cmds, `stg --version`, `stg version`, `stg version --help`-plus-all-its-flags output, `stg version -s`, `stg version` with other flags. Also unknown command: `stg frobnicate` (exact error, exit code), and `stg` with no args. Write an index in /workspace/observed/help.md summarizing where everything is, plus exact outputs of version/unknown-command/no-args cases verbatim in that file.

GROUP=series-inspect. Commands: series, top, next, prev, id, patches, name. Explore all their flags (series: -a -s -A -U -H -m --author -c -i -d -e -P --no-prefix --reverse --short with args, patch ranges as args, patch::range syntax; id: all flags; patches: all flags). Build stacks with applied/unapplied/hidden/empty patches and record exact outputs for every combination, including error cases (empty stack, nothing applied, unknown patch, bad range). Record exit codes and stderr text exactly.

GROUP=push-pop-goto. Commands: pop, push, goto. All flags (pop: -a -s -n; push: -a -n -m/--merged --set-tree --reverse; goto: all flags). Record exact transaction outputs for: popping/pushing single, multiple, all, ranges, by name, from various stack positions; goto to applied/unapplied/topmost patch; errors (no patches applied, no patches to push, already at patch, unknown patch, dirty worktree blocking push with exact error text, push conflict scenario and its output/recovery instructions). Note exit codes and what happens to the worktree. Test how the transaction output compresses ranges vs prints individual lines.

GROUP=new-edit-rename-delete. Commands: new, edit, rename, delete. All flags (new: -m -f -d --author --authdate --committer -t/--topical -r --refname -s/--sign etc; edit: -d -m -t --author --sign --ack --review --edit --diff --save-template etc; rename with old/new names; delete: -t/--top, --branch). Record exact outputs and errors: duplicate patch name, invalid names (what characters are rejected, exact error text), name conflicts with git refs, deleting applied/unapplied/current/only patches, deleting with uncommitted changes that would be lost, new with dirty worktree (does it refuse? --refresh?), new with -m vs editor (avoid interactive editors: use -m always; also test what happens with no -m and no terminal/GIT_EDITOR=false to see failure message). Check sign/ack/review trailer formatting in commit messages.

GROUP=refresh. Command: refresh. All flags: -p/--patch, -u/--update, -i/--index, -s/--subdir, -f/--force, --annotate, -m/--message, -e/--edit, -d/--diff, -a/--author, --authdate, -F/--force-refresh... run refresh --help first. Record: the exact temp-patch transaction output sequence, refreshing a non-top patch (-p) and its exact output, refresh with nothing to refresh (exact error), refresh --index with staged changes only, refresh from subdirectory, refresh with pathspecs, --annotate output (does it add a note?), author/date override behaviors, what happens to patch commit author/committer/message on refresh (inspect git log of the patch commit).

GROUP=float-sink-hide-clean-squash-spill. Commands: float, sink, hide, unhide, clean, squash, spill. All flags. Record exact outputs and errors: float/sink with named patches and with --top/--bottom/--series flags; hide/unhide of applied/unapplied patches (error cases); clean with empty/nonempty patches and -a; squash of 2+ patches (exact output, resulting patch name/message, --name, --save-template, refusal cases like squashing non-contiguous patches or with dirty tree); spill behavior and output. Note resulting stack.json states.

GROUP=commit-uncommit. Commands: commit, uncommit. All flags (commit: -a -n --allow-empty; uncommit: -n -t/--to -x --exclusive -p/--prefix). Set up scenarios: commit 1 patch, commit -a, commit -n 2, commit with no patches (error text), uncommit 2 commits (resulting patch names from commit messages, exact output), uncommit --to, uncommit with prefix, uncommit naming sanitization (commits with spaces/special chars in subject: what patch names result), uncommit more commits than exist (error). Record stack.json and branch HEAD before/after.

GROUP=undo-redo-reset-log-repair. Commands: undo, redo, reset, log, repair. Explore: undo (exact output format, -n, undo past beginning error), redo (same), reset to earlier states (how are states specified), log (default format, -n, -f/--full exact format, -d/--diff exact format, --clear output, log with patch args, -g probably can't test), repair (what it prints when stack is fine; modify branch with plain git commit then repair: exact output and resulting state). Record how undo/redo print the state (they seem to print a multi-line summary of what changed: capture exact text for several undo scenarios: after new, after delete, after pop, after push).

GROUP=show-diff-files-export-import-fold. Commands: show, diff, files, export, import, fold. Explore flags (show: -A -U -H -s and range args; diff: -r/--range, -s/--stat, binary; files: -b/--bare, -s/--stat, -v; export: -d/--dir, -n/--numbered, -t/--template, -e/--stdout, -a/--all... check export --help; import: -m/--mail, -M/--mbox, -s/--series, -u/--url, -n/--name, -t/--stripname, -p/--strip, -i/--ignore-cr, -e/--edit, --replace, -3/--3way; fold: flags). Record exact outputs: show of single/multiple/range patches (it's like git show; capture the exact header format: does it print 'patch <name>' lines?), diff -r variants, files output, export file format (exact file contents: headers, numbering scheme, series file format, stdout mode), import of a diff file (exact output, resulting patch), fold a diff into current patch (output, conflicts).

GROUP=branch-pick-sync. Commands: branch, pick, sync, pull, rebase, email, completion, and the aliases add/mv/rm/status/resolved. branch: --list exact output format (current branch marker), --create, --rename, --cleanup, --protect/--unprotect, --delete (exact outputs/errors, deleting current branch error, protected branch errors), branch with no args. pick: all flags, picking a patch from another branch by name, picking a commit oid, -x/--expose, --name, conflicts, --fold/--update/--revert modes (see pick --help). sync: with --branch/--series, exact outputs and error when patch doesn't exist. pull: behavior without remote (error), maybe with a local file remote. rebase: basic behavior output. email: just help and format/send dry-run errors without sendmail. completion: `stg completion bash`, `stg completion zsh`, `stg completion fish`, `stg completion list` etc — record structure (full scripts are huge; save full output to files under /workspace/observed/completion/ and summarize). aliases: `stg status`, `stg add` behavior (they exec git — verify exact behavior e.g. `stg status` output equals `git status -s`).

GROUP=global-behavior. Investigate cross-cutting behavior of the stg binary: (1) exit codes for success/error/usage-error (bad flag, bad argument) — capture exact stderr for usage errors, e.g. `stg new --bogus`, `stg pop --bogus`, `stg new` when patch name missing... note clap-style error formatting. (2) --color always/never/ansi effects on series and transaction output: capture raw escape bytes (cat -v) for `stg series` with applied/unapplied/hidden/empty patches and for pop/push output. (3) -C flag behavior. (4) Env vars: STGIT_* anything? (test STGIT_AUTHOR? probably not; test GIT_DIR awareness), NO_COLOR. (5) git config knobs: stgit.* settings (e.g. does stgit.autosign exist? test `git config stgit.pick name`... focus on ones observable: stgit.newpage? Just test a few plausible ones and note 'no observable effect' if none). (6) Behavior in subdirectory of repo (output paths relative?), bare repo (error), repo without any commit (stg init error text), detached HEAD (error text for commands needing stack). (7) Patch name validation rules: try names with spaces, slashes, dots, leading dash, '..', control chars, very long names, unicode — record exact error messages. (8) Template files: does `stg new` read .git/.stgit-new.txt or similar? Test creating .stgit-new.txt in repo root and .git, then `stg new` without -m with GIT_EDITOR=false to see if template is used in the failure output... better: GIT_EDITOR=true (no-op) so it uses template verbatim; inspect resulting commit message. Also .stgit-edit.txt for edit. (9) `stg id` formats. (10) How does stg react when refs/stacks/<branch> exists but branch is not current (init -b etc).

Move the specified patches down the stack.

If no patch is specified on the command line, the current (topmost) patch is sunk. By
default, patches are sunk to the bottom of the stack, but the '--above' or '--below'
(alias '--to') options may be used to place them above or below any applied patch.

Internally, sinking involves popping all patches to the bottom (or to the target patch
if '--above' or '--below' is used), then pushing the patches to sink, and then, unless
'--nopush' is specified, pushing back any other formerly applied patches.

Sinking may be useful, for example, to group stable patches at the bottom of the stack
where they less likely to be impacted by the push of another patch, and from where they
can be more easily committed or pushed to another repository.

can have standard mail format. The "Subject", "From", and "Date" headers will be used
for the imported patch's author details.

Patches may also be imported from a mail file (-m/--mail), an mbox (-M/--mbox), or a
series (-S/--series). Furthermore, the -u/--url option allows the patches source to be
fetched from a url instead of from a local file.

If a patch does not apply cleanly import is aborted unless '--reject' is specified, in
which case it will apply to the work tree the parts of the patch that are  applicable,
leave the rejected hunks in corresponding *.rej files, and add an empty patch to the

By default, the imported patch's name is reused, but may be overridden with the '--name'
option. A commit object can be reverted with the '--revert' option.

When using the '--expose' option, the format of the commit message is determined by the

be supplied to the '--pretty' option of 'git show'. The default is "format:%B%n(imported
from commit %H)", which appends the commit hash of the picked commit to the patch's
commit message.

====
Pull the latest changes from a remote repository.

The remote repository may be specified on the command line, but defaults to
branch.<name>.remote from the git configuration, or "origin" if not configured.

This command works by popping all currently applied patches from the stack, pulling the
changes from the remote repository, updating the stack base to the new remote HEAD, and
finally pushing all formerly applied patches back onto the stack. Merge conflicts may
occur during the final push step. Those conflicts need to be resolved manually.

See git-fetch(1) for the format of remote repository argument.

Usage: stg pull [OPTIONS] [repository]

Arguments:
  [repository]
          Repository to pull from

Options:
  -n, --nopush
          Do not push back patches after pulling

  -m, --merged
          Check for patches that may have been merged upstream.
          
          When pushing-back patches, each patch is checked to see if its changes already
          exist in the just-pulled upstream changes. If a patch's changes have already
          been merged upstream, the patch will still exist in the stack, but become
          empty after the pull operation.

      --conflicts[=<policy>]
          Either "allow" or "disallow" pushing a patch with conflicts.
          
          Using `--conflicts=allow` (or just `--conflicts`) allows pushing a patch that
          may result in unresolved merge conflicts. The patch will be pushed and files
          with conflicts will be left with conflict markers to be resolved manually; or
          the operation undone with `stg undo --hard`. This is the default behavior and
          also corresponds to the "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" variable being set to
          "true".
          
          Using `--conflicts=disallow` disallows pushing any patch that would result in
          merge conflicts. The operation will stop on the last patch that can be pushed
          without conflicts. This behavior can be configured by setting
          "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" to "false".

      --color <when>
          Specify when to colorize the output.
          
          `auto` (the default) enables colored output only when outputting to a terminal
          or TTY. The `NO_COLOR` environment variable is respected.
          
          `always` and `never` unconditionlly enable/disable colored output,
          respectively.
          
          `ansi` forces color to be output using ANSI escape sequences, even in a
          Windows console.

          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
====
Pop all patches from the current stack, move the stack base to the given new base and
push the patches back.

Merge conflicts may arise when patches are being pushed-back onto the stack. If this
occurs, resolve the conflicts and then continue the rebase with the following sequence:

    stg add --update
    stg refresh
    stg goto top-patch

Or to skip the conflicting patch:

    stg undo --hard
    stg push next-patch..top-patch

Usage: stg rebase [OPTIONS] [committish]

Arguments:

Options:

          Interactively manipulate patches in editor

  -n, --nopush
          Do not push back patches after rebasing

  -m, --merged
          Check for patches that may have been merged upstream.
          
          When pushing-back patches, each patch is checked to see if its changes already
          exist in the new stack base. If a patch's changes are detected to have been
          merged, the patch will still exist in the stack, but become empty after the
          rebase operation.

      --committer-date-is-author-date
          Instead of using the current time as the committer date, use the author date
          of the commit as the committer date.

      --autostash
          Automatically create a temporary stash before the operation begins, and apply
          it after the operation completes. This allows a rebase to be performed on a
          dirty work tree. Note however that the final stash application may result in
          non-trivial conflicts.

      --conflicts[=<policy>]
          Either "allow" or "disallow" pushing a patch with conflicts.
          
          Using `--conflicts=allow` (or just `--conflicts`) allows pushing a patch that
          may result in unresolved merge conflicts. The patch will be pushed and files
          with conflicts will be left with conflict markers to be resolved manually; or
          the operation undone with `stg undo --hard`. This is the default behavior and
          also corresponds to the "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" variable being set to
          "true".
          
          Using `--conflicts=disallow` disallows pushing any patch that would result in
          merge conflicts. The operation will stop on the last patch that can be pushed
          without conflicts. This behavior can be configured by setting
          "stgit.push.allow-conflicts" to "false".

$STG pop p6 >/dev/null || exit 1
EOF

payload.resultSummary:
Done. Deliverables: `/workspace/observed/help/` (144 capture files) and index `/workspace/observed/help.md`.

Key findings:

- **Full coverage**: captured `--help` and `-h` for all 45 subcommands plus nested ones — `branch --{list,create,clone,rename,protect,unprotect,delete,cleanup,describe}` (branch "subcommands" are literally named with leading dashes), `completion {bash,fish,zsh,list,man}`, `completion list {aliases,commands,commands-and-aliases}`, `email {format,send}`. All exit 0, stdout only.
- **Short vs long help**: `-h` gives one-line-per-option summary; `--help` adds prose paragraphs and multi-line option descriptions. E.g. `new`: 36 vs 134 lines; `import`: 50 vs 150. Clap v4 layout throughout; every leaf command appends a global `--color <when>` and `-h, --help`.
- **Equivalences** (byte-identical, verified with `diff`): `stg help` == `stg --help`; `stg help <cmd>` == `stg <cmd> --help`; `stg version` == `stg --version`; bare `stg` stderr == `stg -h` stdout.
- **Bare `stg`**: exit **1**, short help goes to **stderr** (stdout empty).
- **Unknown command** `stg frobnicate`: exit **1** (not 2!), stderr `error: unrecognized subcommand 'frobnicate'` + blank line + `  tip: a similar subcommand exists: 'float'` + top-level Usage block + `For more information, try '--help'.`
- **`stg help --help` / `-h` fail** (exit 1, "unrecognized subcommand '--help'") — help takes only command names. `stg help help` works. `stg help frobnicate` errors *without* the similarity tip.
- **Version**: 6-line banner `Stacked Git 2.5.5` … `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only` + `git version 2.34.1` (last line is the discovered git version). `-s`/`--short` prints exactly `stg 2.5.5`. No colors even with `--color always`.
- **Edge exits**: `--color bogus` → exit 1 with possible-values list; `-C /nonexistent` → exit **2** (`cannot change to ...: No such file or directory (os error 2)`); `--help` beats `-h` when both given.
- **Quirk**: the binary's long `--color` help contains the typo "unconditionlly" — reproduce verbatim if matching output exactly.
- **Aliases**: `add`, `mv`, `resolved`, `rm`, `status` are git-passthrough aliases; `stg help add` shows `Alias for shell command \`git -C "$GIT_PREFIX" add\`` with `[args]...` passthrough.

All exact byte-level outputs (including the full no-args help text and error blocks) are verbatim in `help.md`; per-command details are in the individual files.

# Observed behavior: `stg series`, `top`, `next`, `prev`, `id`, `patches`, `name`

Binary: StGit 2.5.5 (`/workspace/executable`). All experiments in throwaway repos.
Global notes:

- Exit codes: **0** success; **2** runtime errors (`error: <msg>` on stderr, no usage); **1** CLI/argument-parse errors (clap-style, message + `Usage:` block + `For more information, try '--help'.` on stderr).
- All normal output goes to stdout; `error: ...` lines go to stderr.
- Every command here accepts `-b/--branch <branch>` and `--color <when>` (`auto|always|ansi|never`; `NO_COLOR` env respected in auto mode). `-b` may not be repeated (`error: the argument '--branch <branch>' cannot be used multiple times`, exit 1).
- Detached HEAD: all six commands fail with `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` (exit 2).
- `-b <branch>` where branch ref doesn't exist: `error: branch \`<name>\` not found` (exit 2).
- A branch with **no StGit stack** behaves like an empty stack for `series` (empty output, exit 0) and `top` (`error: no patches applied`), but `name`/`id` with no revision error differently (see below).
- Broken pipe (e.g. `stg series | head -0`): prints `error: Broken pipe (os error 32)` to stderr.

## Test stack used for most experiments

Branch `master`, base = initial empty commit `e581644…`:

- applied: `p1` (adds file-a.txt, msg "first patch", oid 96c971ca…),
  `p2` (file-b.txt, msg "second patch\n\nwith a longer body.", oid 1d1a0e86…),
  `pempty` (empty patch, msg "empty patch", oid a4f72ac5… = stack head)
- unapplied: `p3` (file-c.txt, "third patch", 2c58819e…)
- hidden: `p4` (file-d.txt, "fourth patch", 29663b4e…)
- git config: user.name `Test`, user.email `t@t.com`
- Other branches: `dev` (applied: `p1` *different content/oid, same name*, `devonly`), `other` (applied: `op1`), `nostack` (branch without stack).

---

# `stg series`

Help synopsis:
```
Usage: stg series [OPTIONS] [-A] [-U] [-H]
       stg series [OPTIONS] --all
       stg series [OPTIONS] --short
       stg series [OPTIONS] [patch]...
```
Flags: select: `-a/--all`, `-s/--short[=<n>]`, `-A/--applied`, `-U/--unapplied`, `-H/--hidden`, `-m/--missing <branch>`;
display: `--author`, `-c/--count`, `-i/--commit-id[=<length>]`, `-d/--description`, `-e/--empty`, `-P/--no-prefix`, `-I/--indices`, `-O/--offsets`, `-r/--reverse`, `--showbranch`.

## Basic output

```
$ stg series
+ p1
+ p2
> pempty
- p3
```
- Default shows applied + unapplied, **not hidden**. Prefixes: `+ ` applied, `> ` topmost applied, `- ` unapplied, `! ` hidden. Order: stack bottom first.
- Hidden patches **are** shown when named explicitly as args (or inside an explicit range): `stg series p4` → `! p4`.
- Lines end with `\n`, no extra trailing blank line.
- Empty stack / uninitialized stack: no output, exit 0.

## Select options

- `-a` adds hidden: appends `! p4`. `-A`: applied only. `-U`: unapplied only (`- p3`). `-H`: hidden only (`! p4`).
- `-A -U`, `-A -U -H` combine freely (union, in stack order).
- `-a` conflicts with each of `-A/-U/-H` and with `[patch]...` args: clap error exit 1, e.g.
  `error: the argument '--all' cannot be used with '--applied'` / `... cannot be used with '[patch]...'` (+ usage block).
- `-A/-U/-H` also conflict with `[patch]...` args (same clap error form).
- `-s/--short[=<n>]`: select n patches *around* the topmost applied patch (n below + topmost + n above). `--short=0` → only `> pempty`. `--short=1` (8-patch stack, 4 applied) → pp3,pp4,pp5. Default n (bare `--short` or `-s`) is **5** (with nothing applied and 8 unapplied: shows first 5). Clamps at stack ends.
  - `--short` with nothing applied: reference point is the stack base; shows the first n+1... observed: `--short` → first 5 unapplied; `--short=3` → first 3; `--short=1` → first 1 (`- q1`). (i.e. n patches above the base when none applied — note: with patches applied, n below + top + n above; with none applied it printed exactly n, not 2n+1; with `--short` default it printed 5 = n.)
  - Actually observed with 4 applied / 4 unapplied: `--short=2` → pp2..pp6 (2 below + top + 2 above = 5 lines). With none applied: `--short=3` → pp1..pp3 (3 lines). So window is topmost±n, and "topmost" with none applied = base (excluded), giving just n above.
  - `-s` conflicts with `[patch]...` args: `error: the argument '--short[=<n>]' cannot be used with '[patch]...'` exit 1.
  - `--short=-1` / `--short=abc`: exit 1, `error: invalid value '-1' for '--short[=<n>]': '-1' is not a positive integer` (but `--short=0` is accepted!).
  - `-s2` and `-s=2` are NOT parsed as short-with-value: they fall through to patch args → `error: patch \`-s2\` does not exist` (exit 2). Only `--short=N` (long form with `=`) works.
  - `-s` combined with `-A` is allowed: `stg series -s -A` → applied window only.
- `-m/--missing <branch>`: shows patches present (by **name**) in `<branch>`'s stack but absent by name from the current (or `-b`) branch's stack. Prefixes shown are the *target* branch's statuses; hidden patches of target included only with `-a`. Output order = target stack order. `--showbranch` prefixes target branch name. Empty result → no output exit 0. Unknown branch: `error: branch \`x\` not found` exit 2. Combines with `-A`/patch args (intersection). Verified name-based: `dev` has a different-content patch also named `p1`; from `dev`, `-m master` lists only `p2, pempty, p3` (p1 excluded by name). `-b master -m dev` → `> devonly`.
  - From `other` (stack with only op1), `-m master` listed all 4 master patches.

## Patch args / ranges

Positional args are patch names, absolute indices, relative offsets, or `..` ranges; multiple args must be contiguous and ordered.

- `stg series p1` → `+ p1`. `stg series p1 p2` → both. `pempty p3` (contiguous across applied/unapplied boundary) works.
- Index args: `0` → first patch (p1). `1..2` → p2,pempty. Relative offsets (same convention as `-O`): `+0` → topmost (pempty), `+1` → p3, `-1` → p2, `-2..+1` → p1..p3.
- Ranges: `p1..p3` → p1,p2,pempty,p3. `p1..p1` → just p1. Mixed forms ok: `0..pempty`.
- Open ranges: `..p2` → from stack base through p2. `X..` → from X through the **topmost applied** patch if X is applied (`p1..` → p1,p2,pempty; `pempty..` → just pempty); if X is at/after topmost, runs to the **end of the whole stack including hidden** (`p3..` → `- p3`, `! p4`). `..` alone → base..topmost applied (p1..pempty).
- `..p4` → includes hidden p4 at the end.
- Errors (exit 2):
  - unknown: `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist`
  - reversed range: `error: end patch \`p1\` is out of order with \`p3\``
  - non-contiguous multi args: `error: \`p3\` not contiguous with preceding range \`p1\`` (or `` `p1..p2` ``)
  - reversed multi args: `error: \`p1\` not contiguous with preceding range \`p2\``
  - duplicate: `error: patch \`p1\` is used more than once`
- Errors (exit 1, clap value parser): malformed ranges — `p1::p2`, `p1::2`, `p1...p2`, `.p1`, `p1..p2..p3`, `master:p1` →
  `error: invalid value 'p1::p2' for '[patch]...': invalid patch range \`p1::p2`` + blank line + `For more information, try '--help'.`
  (Note: `branch:patch` syntax is NOT accepted by series args; use `-b`.)

## Display options

- `-P/--no-prefix`: bare names, one per line.
- `-r/--reverse`: top-first order (prefixes unchanged).
- `-e/--empty`: extra leading column: `*` for empty patches, ` ` otherwise, immediately before the prefix char: ` + p1`, `*> pempty`. With `-P`: ` p1` / `*pempty`.
- `-d/--description`: appends padded ` # <first line of message>`; names padded with spaces to align the `#` column:
  ```
  + p1     # first patch
  > pempty # empty patch
  ```
- `--author`: same layout with author **name only** (no email): `+ p2     # Test`. With both `--author -d`: `+ p2 # Test # second patch`.
- `-c/--count`: prints just the number of selected patches (`4`, `5` with -a, `0` on empty stack). Combines with patch args (`-c p1..p3` → `4`).
- `-i/--commit-id[=<length>]`: inserts commit id column between prefix and name: `+ 96c971ca…(full 40) p1    ` (names still padded). `--commit-id=8` → 8 chars; `=4` min; `=41` clamps to full 40; `=3` → exit 1 `error: invalid value '3' for '--commit-id[=<length>]': length must be "full" or an integer greater than or equal to 4`. `-i 8` (space) is parsed as patch arg `8` → `error: invalid patch index \`8\`` exit 2. Bare `-i` = full id.
- `-I/--indices`: column of absolute indices: `+ 0 p1`, `> 2 pempty`.
- `-O/--offsets`: column of signed offsets from topmost applied (`+0` = topmost): `+ -2 p1`, `> +0 pempty`, `- +1 p3`. With nothing applied, offsets count from the base: `- +1 q1`, `- +2 q2`.
- Combined column order: `<empty-col><prefix> <index> <offset> <commit-id> <name> # <author> # <description>`:
  ```
   + 0 -2 96c971ca… p1     # Test # first patch
  *> 2 +0 a4f72ac5… pempty # Test # empty patch
  ```
- `--showbranch`: name shown as `<branch>:<name>` (the `-b` branch when given). With `-P`: `master:p1` etc. without status prefix.

## Colors (`--color always`, via `cat -v`)

`stg series --color always -a -d -e` produced (ESC shown as ^[):
```
 ^[[0m^[[32m+ ^[[0m^[[0mp1    ^[[0m^[[38;5;8m #^[[0m first patch^[[0m
^[[0m^[[36m*^[[0m^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[0m^[[1mpempty^[[0m^[[1m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[1m empty patch^[[0m
 ^[[0m^[[35m- ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2mp3    ^[[0m^[[2m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[2m third patch^[[0m
 ^[[0m^[[31m! ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2m^[[3mp4    ^[[0m^[[2m^[[3m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[2m^[[3m fourth patch^[[0m
```
Summary of styles:
- `+ ` prefix: green (32); applied name: no style.
- `> ` prefix: blue (34); topmost name: bold (1).
- `- ` prefix: magenta (35); unapplied name: dim (2).
- `! ` prefix: red (31); hidden name: dim+italic (2;3).
- empty-marker `*`: cyan (36).
- ` #` separator: bright-black/grey `38;5;8` for plain patches; `1;30` for topmost, `2;30` for unapplied, `2;3;30` for hidden (matches name style + black). Description text itself takes the name style (bold/dim/dim-italic) or none.
- Each colored segment is wrapped in its own `ESC[0m` … `ESC[0m` resets.
- `stg top --color always` → `^[[0m^[[1mpempty^[[0m` (bold name only).
- `--color=bad` → exit 1: `error: invalid value 'bad' for '--color <when>'\n  [possible values: auto, always, ansi, never]`.

## Misc series cases

- From a subdirectory: works identically (paths/branch resolution from repo root).
- Uninitialized repo (no stack ref): `series` → empty output exit 0 (even `-a`, `-c` → `0`).

---

# `stg top` / `stg next` / `stg prev`

No extra flags (any positional arg → exit 1 `error: unexpected argument 'extra' found`).

- `stg top` → `pempty` (name + `\n`). None applied → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- `stg next` → `p3` (first unapplied). All applied → `error: no unapplied patches` exit 2. None applied but unapplied exist → first one (`q1`), exit 0. Hidden patches are never "next".
- `stg prev` → `p2` (patch below topmost). Only one applied → `error: not enough patches applied` exit 2. None applied → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- `-b` works for all three (`top -b dev` → `devonly`, `prev -b dev` → `p1`, `next -b other` → error `no unapplied patches`).
- No `--showbranch` on these.

---

# `stg id [revision]`

Resolves an StGit-aware revspec to a full 40-hex oid on stdout. No revision → current branch's **HEAD commit** oid (exit 0) — even on an uninitialized stack (prints branch head).

Revspec forms:
- `<patch>`: patch commit oid (works for applied, unapplied, hidden).
- `[<branch>:]{base}`: stack base commit (`{base}`, `master:{base}`). For a branch with no stack: branch head.
- `<patch>^`, `<patch>~1`, `other:op1^`: parent commits (resolved via git revparse semantics).
- Plain git revspecs: `HEAD`, `HEAD~1`, `@`, `master`, `refs/heads/master`, `HEAD^{tree}` (prints tree oid), full/short oids.
- `-b other op1`: patch names resolved against `-b` branch. `-b other p1` (p1 not in other's stack) → `error: patch \`p1\` does not exist` exit 2.

Errors:
- unknown patch: `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist` exit 2.
- too-deep ancestry: `stg id p1~2` → `error: finding ancestor: repository does not have enough commit depth` exit 2.
- two args: exit 1 `error: unexpected argument 'p2' found`.
- unparseable revspec: exit 1, clap value error with caret diagnostics:
  ```
  error: invalid value '???' for '[revision]': invalid StGit revision `???`: ???
  ^
  ```
  (followed by two blank lines and `For more information, try '--help'.`; same for empty string arg.)

---

# `stg name [revision]`

Inverse of `id`: maps a revision to a patch name in the current (or `-b`) branch's stack.

- No revision → name of topmost applied patch (`pempty`). On an initialized stack with nothing applied → `{base}` (exit 0). On a branch with **no stack at all** → `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch \`master\`` exit 2 (this differs from `id`, which works uninitialized).
- `name p1` → `p1`; works for unapplied (`p3`) and hidden (`p4`) patches.
- `name p1^` / `name {base}` → `{base}`.
- Any git revspec or raw oid matching a patch commit → that patch's name: `name HEAD` → `pempty`, `name HEAD~2` → `p1`, `name 96c971ca…` → `p1`.
- Oid not corresponding to any patch/base in the looked-up stack → `error: patch name not found for revision \`<oid>\`` exit 2. Notably `name other:op1` from master fails this way (the revision resolves fine, but name lookup happens in the *current* branch's stack). `name -b other` → `op1`.
- `--showbranch` → `master:p1`, `master:pempty` (also for no-arg).
- Unknown patch name → `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist` exit 2.

---

# `stg patches [path]... [-d] [-O <diff-opt>]...`

Shows **applied** patches (of current or `-b` branch) that modify the given paths; without path args, uses files with local (worktree or index) modifications.

- `stg patches file-a.txt` → `p1`. Multiple paths: union, one name per line, in stack order (`file-a.txt file-b.txt` → `p1`, `p2`). Duplicates removed (`file-a.txt file-a.txt` → `p1` once).
- Unapplied/hidden patches are never listed (`file-c.txt`, `file-d.txt` → empty output, exit 0). Nonexistent path → empty, exit 0. `patches .` → p1, p2.
- No args + dirty tracked file `file-a.txt` → `p1`. No args + only an *untracked* file → `error: no local changes and no paths specified` exit 2. No args + only *staged* new file → empty output, exit 0 (index changes count as local changes). No applied patches at all → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- Works from a subdirectory with `../file-a.txt`.
- `-b dev devfile.txt` → `p1` (dev's p1).
- `-d/--diff`: for each matching patch prints (exact format; separator is **50 dashes**):
  ```
  --------------------------------------------------
  p1
  --------------------------------------------------
  first patch

  ---
  diff --git a/file-a.txt b/file-a.txt
  new file mode 100644
  index 0000000..72943a1
  --- a/file-a.txt
  +++ b/file-a.txt
  @@ -0,0 +1 @@
  +aaa
  ```
  The full commit message (including body, e.g. "second patch\n\nwith a longer body.") is printed, then blank line, then `---`, then the diff of that patch restricted to the given paths. Multiple matches → sections concatenated directly (next `----` line immediately after previous diff, no blank line).
- `-O/--diff-opt <option>` (repeatable): passed to the underlying `git diff-tree`. With `-d -O --stat` → stat output followed by blank line then the full diff as well (i.e. `--stat` is added; patch output still present — observed both). `-d -O --name-only` → only the filename list (replaces patch output). `-O` **without** `-d` has no effect — even a bogus option is silently ignored (exit 0). With `-d`, a bogus option prints the partial header to stdout and git's usage text to stderr:
  `error: \`git diff-tree\`: usage: git diff-tree ...` exit 2 (full usage text follows on stderr).

---

# Quick error-message reference (all exit 2 unless noted)

| Command | Message |
|---|---|
| series/top/next/prev/id/name/patches (detached) | `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` |
| any, bad `-b` | `error: branch \`nosuchbranch\` not found` |
| series, unknown patch | `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist` |
| series, bad order | `error: end patch \`p1\` is out of order with \`p3\`` |
| series, non-contiguous | `error: \`p3\` not contiguous with preceding range \`p1\`` |
| series, dup | `error: patch \`p1\` is used more than once` |
| series, malformed range | exit 1: `error: invalid value '…' for '[patch]...': invalid patch range \`…\`` |
| top (none applied) | `error: no patches applied` |
| prev (1 applied) | `error: not enough patches applied` |
| next (all applied) | `error: no unapplied patches` |
| name, no stack | `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch \`master\`` |
| name, oid not in stack | `error: patch name not found for revision \`<oid>\`` |
| id, too deep | `error: finding ancestor: repository does not have enough commit depth` |
| id, bad revspec | exit 1: `error: invalid value '???' for '[revision]': invalid StGit revision \`???\`: ???` + caret line |
| patches, no changes/paths | `error: no local changes and no paths specified` |
| patches, none applied | `error: no patches applied` |
| clap conflicts/unexpected args | exit 1, `error: the argument '--all' cannot be used with '--applied'` / `error: unexpected argument 'extra' found` (+ Usage block) |
EOF
wc -l /workspace/observed/series-inspect.md

  - From `other` (stack with only op1), `-m master` listed all 4 master patches.

## Patch args / ranges

Positional args are patch names, absolute indices, relative offsets, or `..` ranges; multiple args must be contiguous and ordered.

- `stg series p1` → `+ p1`. `stg series p1 p2` → both. `pempty p3` (contiguous across applied/unapplied boundary) works.
- Index args: `0` → first patch (p1). `1..2` → p2,pempty. Relative offsets (same convention as `-O`): `+0` → topmost (pempty), `+1` → p3, `-1` → p2, `-2..+1` → p1..p3.
- Ranges: `p1..p3` → p1,p2,pempty,p3. `p1..p1` → just p1. Mixed forms ok: `0..pempty`.
- Open ranges: `..p2` → from stack base through p2. `X..` → from X through the **topmost applied** patch if X is applied (`p1..` → p1,p2,pempty; `pempty..` → just pempty); if X is at/after topmost, runs to the **end of the whole stack including hidden** (`p3..` → `- p3`, `! p4`). `..` alone → base..topmost applied (p1..pempty).
- `..p4` → includes hidden p4 at the end.
- Errors (exit 2):
  - unknown: `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist`
  - reversed range: `error: end patch \`p1\` is out of order with \`p3\``
  - non-contiguous multi args: `error: \`p3\` not contiguous with preceding range \`p1\`` (or `` `p1..p2` ``)
  - reversed multi args: `error: \`p1\` not contiguous with preceding range \`p2\``
  - duplicate: `error: patch \`p1\` is used more than once`
- Errors (exit 1, clap value parser): malformed ranges — `p1::p2`, `p1::2`, `p1...p2`, `.p1`, `p1..p2..p3`, `master:p1` →
  `error: invalid value 'p1::p2' for '[patch]...': invalid patch range \`p1::p2`` + blank line + `For more information, try '--help'.`
  (Note: `branch:patch` syntax is NOT accepted by series args; use `-b`.)

## Display options

- `-P/--no-prefix`: bare names, one per line.
- `-r/--reverse`: top-first order (prefixes unchanged).
- `-e/--empty`: extra leading column: `*` for empty patches, ` ` otherwise, immediately before the prefix char: ` + p1`, `*> pempty`. With `-P`: ` p1` / `*pempty`.
- `-d/--description`: appends padded ` # <first line of message>`; names padded with spaces to align the `#` column:
  ```
  + p1     # first patch
  > pempty # empty patch
  ```
- `--author`: same layout with author **name only** (no email): `+ p2     # Test`. With both `--author -d`: `+ p2 # Test # second patch`.
- `-c/--count`: prints just the number of selected patches (`4`, `5` with -a, `0` on empty stack). Combines with patch args (`-c p1..p3` → `4`).
- `-i/--commit-id[=<length>]`: inserts commit id column between prefix and name: `+ 96c971ca…(full 40) p1    ` (names still padded). `--commit-id=8` → 8 chars; `=4` min; `=41` clamps to full 40; `=3` → exit 1 `error: invalid value '3' for '--commit-id[=<length>]': length must be "full" or an integer greater than or equal to 4`. `-i 8` (space) is parsed as patch arg `8` → `error: invalid patch index \`8\`` exit 2. Bare `-i` = full id.
- `-I/--indices`: column of absolute indices: `+ 0 p1`, `> 2 pempty`.
- `-O/--offsets`: column of signed offsets from topmost applied (`+0` = topmost): `+ -2 p1`, `> +0 pempty`, `- +1 p3`. With nothing applied, offsets count from the base: `- +1 q1`, `- +2 q2`.
- Combined column order: `<empty-col><prefix> <index> <offset> <commit-id> <name> # <author> # <description>`:
  ```
   + 0 -2 96c971ca… p1     # Test # first patch
  *> 2 +0 a4f72ac5… pempty # Test # empty patch
  ```
- `--showbranch`: name shown as `<branch>:<name>` (the `-b` branch when given). With `-P`: `master:p1` etc. without status prefix.

## Colors (`--color always`, via `cat -v`)

`stg series --color always -a -d -e` produced (ESC shown as ^[):
```
 ^[[0m^[[32m+ ^[[0m^[[0mp1    ^[[0m^[[38;5;8m #^[[0m first patch^[[0m
^[[0m^[[36m*^[[0m^[[0m^[[34m> ^[[0m^[[0m^[[1mpempty^[[0m^[[1m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[1m empty patch^[[0m
 ^[[0m^[[35m- ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2mp3    ^[[0m^[[2m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[2m third patch^[[0m
 ^[[0m^[[31m! ^[[0m^[[0m^[[2m^[[3mp4    ^[[0m^[[2m^[[3m^[[30m #^[[0m^[[2m^[[3m fourth patch^[[0m
```
Summary of styles:
- `+ ` prefix: green (32); applied name: no style.
- `> ` prefix: blue (34); topmost name: bold (1).
- `- ` prefix: magenta (35); unapplied name: dim (2).
- `! ` prefix: red (31); hidden name: dim+italic (2;3).
- empty-marker `*`: cyan (36).
- ` #` separator: bright-black/grey `38;5;8` for plain patches; `1;30` for topmost, `2;30` for unapplied, `2;3;30` for hidden (matches name style + black). Description text itself takes the name style (bold/dim/dim-italic) or none.
- Each colored segment is wrapped in its own `ESC[0m` … `ESC[0m` resets.
- `stg top --color always` → `^[[0m^[[1mpempty^[[0m` (bold name only).
- `--color=bad` → exit 1: `error: invalid value 'bad' for '--color <when>'\n  [possible values: auto, always, ansi, never]`.

## Misc series cases

- From a subdirectory: works identically (paths/branch resolution from repo root).
- Uninitialized repo (no stack ref): `series` → empty output exit 0 (even `-a`, `-c` → `0`).

---

# `stg top` / `stg next` / `stg prev`

No extra flags (any positional arg → exit 1 `error: unexpected argument 'extra' found`).

- `stg top` → `pempty` (name + `\n`). None applied → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- `stg next` → `p3` (first unapplied). All applied → `error: no unapplied patches` exit 2. None applied but unapplied exist → first one (`q1`), exit 0. Hidden patches are never "next".
- `stg prev` → `p2` (patch below topmost). Only one applied → `error: not enough patches applied` exit 2. None applied → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- `-b` works for all three (`top -b dev` → `devonly`, `prev -b dev` → `p1`, `next -b other` → error `no unapplied patches`).
- No `--showbranch` on these.

---

# `stg id [revision]`

Resolves an StGit-aware revspec to a full 40-hex oid on stdout. No revision → current branch's **HEAD commit** oid (exit 0) — even on an uninitialized stack (prints branch head).

Revspec forms:
- `<patch>`: patch commit oid (works for applied, unapplied, hidden).
- `[<branch>:]{base}`: stack base commit (`{base}`, `master:{base}`). For a branch with no stack: branch head.
- `<patch>^`, `<patch>~1`, `other:op1^`: parent commits (resolved via git revparse semantics).
- Plain git revspecs: `HEAD`, `HEAD~1`, `@`, `master`, `refs/heads/master`, `HEAD^{tree}` (prints tree oid), full/short oids.
- `-b other op1`: patch names resolved against `-b` branch. `-b other p1` (p1 not in other's stack) → `error: patch \`p1\` does not exist` exit 2.

Errors:
- unknown patch: `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist` exit 2.
- too-deep ancestry: `stg id p1~2` → `error: finding ancestor: repository does not have enough commit depth` exit 2.
- two args: exit 1 `error: unexpected argument 'p2' found`.
- unparseable revspec: exit 1, clap value error with caret diagnostics:
  ```
  error: invalid value '???' for '[revision]': invalid StGit revision `???`: ???
  ^
  ```
  (followed by two blank lines and `For more information, try '--help'.`; same for empty string arg.)

---

# `stg name [revision]`

Inverse of `id`: maps a revision to a patch name in the current (or `-b`) branch's stack.

- No revision → name of topmost applied patch (`pempty`). On an initialized stack with nothing applied → `{base}` (exit 0). On a branch with **no stack at all** → `error: StGit stack not initialized for branch \`master\`` exit 2 (this differs from `id`, which works uninitialized).
- `name p1` → `p1`; works for unapplied (`p3`) and hidden (`p4`) patches.
- `name p1^` / `name {base}` → `{base}`.
- Any git revspec or raw oid matching a patch commit → that patch's name: `name HEAD` → `pempty`, `name HEAD~2` → `p1`, `name 96c971ca…` → `p1`.
- Oid not corresponding to any patch/base in the looked-up stack → `error: patch name not found for revision \`<oid>\`` exit 2. Notably `name other:op1` from master fails this way (the revision resolves fine, but name lookup happens in the *current* branch's stack). `name -b other` → `op1`.
- `--showbranch` → `master:p1`, `master:pempty` (also for no-arg).
- Unknown patch name → `error: patch \`nonexistent\` does not exist` exit 2.

---

# `stg patches [path]... [-d] [-O <diff-opt>]...`

Shows **applied** patches (of current or `-b` branch) that modify the given paths; without path args, uses files with local (worktree or index) modifications.

- `stg patches file-a.txt` → `p1`. Multiple paths: union, one name per line, in stack order (`file-a.txt file-b.txt` → `p1`, `p2`). Duplicates removed (`file-a.txt file-a.txt` → `p1` once).
- Unapplied/hidden patches are never listed (`file-c.txt`, `file-d.txt` → empty output, exit 0). Nonexistent path → empty, exit 0. `patches .` → p1, p2.
- No args + dirty tracked file `file-a.txt` → `p1`. No args + only an *untracked* file → `error: no local changes and no paths specified` exit 2. No args + only *staged* new file → empty output, exit 0 (index changes count as local changes). No applied patches at all → `error: no patches applied` exit 2.
- Works from a subdirectory with `../file-a.txt`.
- `-b dev devfile.txt` → `p1` (dev's p1).
- `-d/--diff`: for each matching patch prints (exact format; separator is **50 dashes**):
  ```
  --------------------------------------------------
  p1
  --------------------------------------------------
  first patch

  ---
  diff --git a/file-a.txt b/file-a.txt
  new file mode 100644
  index 0000000..72943a1
  --- a/file-a.txt
  +++ b/file-a.txt
  @@ -0,0 +1 @@
  +aaa
  ```
  The full commit message (including body, e.g. "second patch\n\nwith a longer body.") is printed, then blank line, then `---`, then the diff of that patch restricted to the given paths. Multiple matches → sections concatenated directly (next `----` line immediately after previous diff, no blank line).
- `-O/--diff-opt <option>` (repeatable): passed to the underlying `git diff-tree`. With `-d -O --stat` → stat output followed by blank line then the full diff as well (i.e. `--stat` is added; patch output still present — observed both). `-d -O --name-only` → only the filename list (replaces patch output). `-O` **without** `-d` has no effect — even a bogus option is silently ignored (exit 0). With `-d`, a bogus option prints the partial header to stdout and git's usage text to stderr:
  `error: \`git diff-tree\`: usage: git diff-tree ...` exit 2 (full usage text follows on stderr).

payload.resultSummary:
Spec written to `/workspace/observed/series-inspect.md`. Key findings:

**Global**
- Exit codes: 0 ok, **2** runtime errors (`error: <msg>` on stderr), **1** clap/arg-parse errors (with Usage block). Unusual that parse errors are 1, not 2.
- Detached HEAD → `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` for all six commands. Unknown `-b` branch → `error: branch \`x\` not found`.
- `series` works on uninitialized stacks (empty output, exit 0); `name` without a stack errors `StGit stack not initialized for branch \`master\``.

**series**
- Default hides hidden patches, but hidden patches appear when explicitly named or ranged (`series p4` → `! p4`).
- Patch args accept names, absolute indices (`0`), and signed offsets (`+0`=topmost, `-1`, matching `-O` column semantics).
- Open range `X..` ends at topmost applied if X is applied (`p1..` → p1..pempty), but at end-of-stack *including hidden* if X is unapplied (`p3..` → p3, p4). `..` alone = base..topmost.
- `-s/--short` default n=5; only `--short=N` works (`-s2`, `-s=2` fall through to patch args → "patch `-s2` does not exist"). `--short=0` allowed despite parser calling values "positive integer".
- `-m <branch>` compares by patch **name** (a different patch with same name counts as present); shows target branch's statuses; combinable with `-b`, `-A`, patch args.
- `branch:patch` syntax is rejected in series args (exit 1 "invalid patch range").
- Column order with all display flags: `<*><prefix> <idx> <offset> <oid> <name> # <author> # <description>`; `--author` prints name only, no email. `-i` bare = full 40-hex; `--commit-id=41` clamps to 40.
- Colors: `+` green, `>` blue + bold name, `-` magenta + dim name, `!` red + dim-italic name, `*` cyan, `#` separator grey/30 with name's style; each segment individually reset-wrapped. Full raw escape sequences in the spec.

**top/next/prev**: name only; prev with 1 applied → `error: not enough patches applied`; next ignores hidden.

**id**: no arg = HEAD oid (works uninitialized); supports `<patch>^`, `[branch:]{base}`, arbitrary git revspecs incl `^{tree}`; bad revspec gives exit-1 caret diagnostics.

**name**: resolves any oid to a patch in the *lookup* branch's stack — `name other:op1` from master fails with `error: patch name not found for revision \`<oid>\``. No-arg on empty stack → `{base}`.

**patches**: applied patches only; no-args mode uses worktree/index changes (staged-only counts as changes → empty output exit 0; untracked-only → `error: no local changes and no paths specified`). `-d` format: 50-dash separator / name / 50-dash / full message / blank / `---` / diff. `-O` is silently ignored without `-d` (even bogus options); with `-d`, `--stat` still also prints the full diff.

args.command:
cat > /workspace/observed/refresh.md <<'SPEC_EOF'
# `stg refresh` — observed behavior spec (StGit 2.5.5 reference binary)

All observations from running `/workspace/executable` (StGit 2.5.5) in throwaway repos.
Git identity: `Test <t@t.com>`. Exit codes noted per case. `stg refresh` has **no**
`-b/--branch` option and no `--subdir` option (the task brief listed those; they don't
exist — `-s` is `--signoff`, `-F` is `--force`, `-f` is `--file`).

## Usage / flags (from `stg refresh --help`)

```
Usage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...

Arguments:
  [path]...                         Only refresh files matching path

Refresh Options:
  -u, --update                      Only update the current patch files
  -i, --index                       Set patch top to index contents instead of worktree
  -F, --force                       Force full refresh even when index is dirty
      --conflicts[=<policy>]        "allow" (default) or "disallow"
  -p, --patch <patch>               Refresh (applied) <patch> instead of the top patch
  -a, --annotate <note>             Annotate the patch log entry with <note>
      --submodules / --no-submodules

Patch Edit Options:
  -e, --edit                        Invoke editor for patch description
  -d, --diff                        Show diff when editing patch description
  -m, --message <message>           Use message instead of invoking the editor
  -f, --file <path>                 Read message from file ("-" = stdin)
      --no-verify                   Disable commit-msg hook
  -s, --signoff[=<value>]           Add Signed-off-by trailer (repeatable)
      --ack[=<value>]               Add Acked-by trailer (repeatable)
      --review[=<value>]            Add Reviewed-by trailer (repeatable)
      --author <name-and-email>
      --authname <name>
      --authemail <email>
      --authdate <date>             "now" = current time
      --committer-date-is-author-date
```
Plus global `--color <when>` (auto/always/never/ansi), `-h/--help`.

## Core mechanism

Refresh works via a **temporary patch**:
1. A new patch named `refresh-temp` (first free of `refresh-temp`, `refresh-temp-1`,
   `refresh-temp-2`, ...) is created on top of the current top, containing the changes
   to be refreshed. Temp commit message is exactly `Refresh of <target-patch-name>`
   with **no trailing newline**; author/committer = current user @ current time.
2. If the target patch is not the top, patches above it (incl. the temp) are popped,
   the temp is pushed at the target's position.
3. The temp patch is popped and merged ("squashed") into the target patch, which is
   rewritten (new commit).
4. Patches above are re-pushed.

Two stack-log entries per refresh:
- `refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)`
- `refresh <target>`  (or `refresh  (CONFLICT)` on conflict — note two spaces; or
  `refresh` when aborting with `--conflicts=disallow`)

So `stg undo` once → back to state with temp patch applied on top; twice → original
state. `--annotate <note>` is appended as the body of the `refresh <target>` log-entry
commit message only (`refresh p1\n\nmy annotation note`); visible in `stg log -f`,
not in plain `stg log`.

## Transaction output markers

stdout, one per line:
- `> <name> (new)` — temp patch created (topmost)
- `- <name>` / `- <first>..<last>` — patch(es) popped (range when >1)
- `> <name>` — patch pushed, now topmost
- `+ <name>` — patch pushed, not topmost
- `# <name>` — temp patch merged away (deleted)
- `& <name>` — target patch updated (rewritten with temp's changes)
- `old => new` — patch renamed (only via editor `Patch:` header)
- Suffixes: ` (new)`, ` (empty)`, ` (conflict)` appended after the name.
- Conflict file status lines (e.g. `UU c.txt`) printed on stdout after the conflict line.

### Canonical sequences (verbatim stdout)

Refresh top patch, with changes:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
> p1
```
Exit 0. If the refreshed commit is identical (clean worktree, no message options),
the `& p1` line is omitted, the commit is **not** rewritten, exit still 0:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
> p1
```

Refresh non-top applied patch (`stg refresh -p p1`, p1 below p2,p3):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
+ p2
> p3
```
(Patches above target popped together with temp in one range, temp pushed at target
position, merged, then others re-pushed. Pushed empty patches get ` (empty)` suffix,
e.g. `+ refresh-temp (empty)`. If the temp ends up empty at the target position the
topmost line reads `> refresh-temp (empty)` and `&` is omitted.)

Refresh an **unapplied** patch (`-p` accepts unapplied patches; works even with all
patches popped, provided the temp patch is creatable from worktree vs HEAD):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
& p2
# refresh-temp
> p1
```
Note order: `& <target>` **before** `# refresh-temp`; trailing `> p1` only if there is
an applied topmost patch (omitted when all popped). If nothing changed, the `&` line
is omitted too.

## Dirty-index check

- Staged-only changes (worktree == index ≠ HEAD): refresh proceeds, no warning.
- Unstaged-only changes: proceeds.
- Staged **and** unstaged changes present (any files, even different files):
  ```
  error: the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`
  ```
  stderr, exit 2, no output on stdout, no side effects. `-F/--force` or `-i/--index`
  override. Untracked files don't count as changes and are never refreshed.

## `--index` / `--update` / pathspecs

- `--index`: patch top set to index contents; unstaged worktree changes preserved.
- `-u/--update`: only files already in the target patch are refreshed; other staged
  files stay staged. (Dirty-index check still applies.)
- Pathspecs are relative to **cwd**; only matching files are refreshed, the rest stay
  staged/unstaged. Pathspec matching nothing → success (exit 0), output without `&`.
- Running from a subdirectory with **no** pathspec refreshes everything (cwd does not
  limit scope).
- Deletions (staged `git rm` or unstaged `rm`) are refreshed like other changes.

## Errors (stderr, exit codes)

| Case | Message | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| No applied patches (default target) | `error: no patches applied` | 2 |
| `-p` nonexistent | ``error: patch `nosuch` does not exist`` | 2 |
| `-p` hidden patch | ``error: hidden patch `p2` is not allowed`` | 2 |
| Detached HEAD | `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` | 2 |
| `-p branch:name` syntax | `error: invalid value 'other:op' for '--patch <patch>': invalid patch locator ` + backtick-quoted `other:op` + `\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--authdate` | `error: invalid value 'garbage' for '--authdate <date>': invalid date `garbage`` + blank + `For more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--author` | `error: invalid value 'NoEmail' for '--author <name-and-email>': invalid name and email `NoEmail`` + help line | 1 |
| `-m` twice | `error: the argument '--message <message>' cannot be used multiple times` + `\n\nUsage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| `-m ""` | `error: a value is required for '--message <message>' but none was supplied` + help line | 1 |
| Merge conflict (allow) | `error: merge conflicts; resolve conflicts manually then refresh or undo the operation with `stg undo --hard`.` | 3 |
| `--conflicts=disallow` | ``error: pushing patch `refresh-temp` would result in conflicts and push conflicts are disallowed`` | 3 |
| commit-msg hook fails | `<hook stderr>` then ``error: `commit-msg` hook returned 1`` | 2 |
| Empty message from editor | `error: aborting due to empty patch description` | 2 |
| Editor fails to run | `error: running editor: vi: No such file or directory (os error 2)` (falls back to `vi` when no EDITOR) | 2 |

## Conflict behavior (`refresh -p p1` conflicting with p2 above)

stdout:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp (conflict)
UU c.txt
```
stderr: `error: merge conflicts; ...` (above), exit 3.
State: temp patch left **applied and topmost**, patches above target unapplied
(`+ p1`, `> refresh-temp`, `- p2`); stack-log entry `refresh  (CONFLICT)`.
Conflict markers: `<<<<<<< current` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> patched`.
Resolution flow: fix files, `git add`, plain `stg refresh` (refreshes the temp patch,
new temp named `refresh-temp-1`), then `stg squash`/`stg push` etc.

With `--conflicts=disallow` (or `stgit.push.allow-conflicts=false`): stdout stops at
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
```
exit 3, temp patch left **unapplied** in the stack, target topmost applied.

On aborts (hook failure, empty editor message, editor spawn failure): only
`> refresh-temp (new)` is printed and the temp patch remains applied/topmost.

## Commit rewriting semantics

- Plain refresh preserves author name/email/date of the original patch commit;
  committer = current user, committer date = now.
- `--author "N <e>"`, `--authname`, `--authemail`, `--authdate` (accepts e.g.
  `2001-02-03T04:05:06`, `1999-12-31 23:59:59`, `now`) override the corresponding
  author fields; unspecified fields keep previous values.
- `--committer-date-is-author-date`: committer timestamp = author timestamp.
- `-m/--message`, `-f/--file` (`-` = stdin), `-e/--edit` replace the patch message.
  `-m` with no content changes still rewrites the commit (`&` shown).
- Trailers: `-s/--signoff`, `--ack`, `--review` default to committer identity; custom
  values require `=` syntax (`--signoff="Custom Signer <cs@x.com>"`) — a space-separated
  value is treated as a pathspec positional. Appended to existing trailers; exact
  duplicate trailers are suppressed (repeat `-s -s` adds one).
- `stgit.autosign` config: no effect observed on refresh.
- Resulting patch may become empty — allowed, kept in stack.

## Editor (`-e`)

- `hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...` printed to **stderr**.
- Editor template:
  ```
  Patch:  p1
  Author: Test <t@t.com>
  Date:   2026-08-07 12:17:06 +0000

  <current message>

  # Please enter the message for your patch. Lines starting with
  # '#' will be ignored. An empty message aborts the new patch.
  # The patch name and author information may also be modified.
  # The diff below is for reference. Any edits will be ignored.
  # ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
  # Do not modify or remove the line above.
  <diff, only with -d>
  ```
- Editing the `Patch:` header renames the patch: output gains `p1 => renamed` after
  the `& p1` line and ends `> renamed`.
- Editing `Author:` header changes the author.
- `-d` appends the **full patch diff** (40-char blob hashes) after the `>8` cut line;
  `-d` without `-e` is silently ignored.
- `-m` + `-e`: editor starts from the `-m` message.
- Empty resulting message → abort (exit 2, temp patch left).

## commit-msg hook

- Runs **only when message options are given** (`-m`/`-e`/`-f`/trailers), once, on a
  temp file `.stgit-msg-temp-<pid>` in the repo root (removed afterwards); hook edits
  to the file take effect. Does not run on plain content-only refresh. `--no-verify`
  skips it. Nonzero hook exit aborts (exit 2, temp patch left applied).

Plus global `--color <when>` (auto/always/never/ansi), `-h/--help`.

## Core mechanism

Refresh works via a **temporary patch**:
1. A new patch named `refresh-temp` (first free of `refresh-temp`, `refresh-temp-1`,
   `refresh-temp-2`, ...) is created on top of the current top, containing the changes
   to be refreshed. Temp commit message is exactly `Refresh of <target-patch-name>`
   with **no trailing newline**; author/committer = current user @ current time.
2. If the target patch is not the top, patches above it (incl. the temp) are popped,
   the temp is pushed at the target's position.
3. The temp patch is popped and merged ("squashed") into the target patch, which is
   rewritten (new commit).
4. Patches above are re-pushed.

Two stack-log entries per refresh:
- `refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)`
- `refresh <target>`  (or `refresh  (CONFLICT)` on conflict — note two spaces; or
  `refresh` when aborting with `--conflicts=disallow`)

So `stg undo` once → back to state with temp patch applied on top; twice → original
state. `--annotate <note>` is appended as the body of the `refresh <target>` log-entry
commit message only (`refresh p1\n\nmy annotation note`); visible in `stg log -f`,
not in plain `stg log`.

## Transaction output markers

stdout, one per line:
- `> <name> (new)` — temp patch created (topmost)
- `- <name>` / `- <first>..<last>` — patch(es) popped (range when >1)
- `> <name>` — patch pushed, now topmost
- `+ <name>` — patch pushed, not topmost
- `# <name>` — temp patch merged away (deleted)
- `& <name>` — target patch updated (rewritten with temp's changes)
- `old => new` — patch renamed (only via editor `Patch:` header)
- Suffixes: ` (new)`, ` (empty)`, ` (conflict)` appended after the name.
- Conflict file status lines (e.g. `UU c.txt`) printed on stdout after the conflict line.

### Canonical sequences (verbatim stdout)

Refresh top patch, with changes:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
> p1
```
Exit 0. If the refreshed commit is identical (clean worktree, no message options),
the `& p1` line is omitted, the commit is **not** rewritten, exit still 0:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
> p1
```

Refresh non-top applied patch (`stg refresh -p p1`, p1 below p2,p3):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
+ p2
> p3
```
(Patches above target popped together with temp in one range, temp pushed at target
position, merged, then others re-pushed. Pushed empty patches get ` (empty)` suffix,
e.g. `+ refresh-temp (empty)`. If the temp ends up empty at the target position the
topmost line reads `> refresh-temp (empty)` and `&` is omitted.)

Refresh an **unapplied** patch (`-p` accepts unapplied patches; works even with all
patches popped, provided the temp patch is creatable from worktree vs HEAD):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
& p2
# refresh-temp
> p1
```
Note order: `& <target>` **before** `# refresh-temp`; trailing `> p1` only if there is
an applied topmost patch (omitted when all popped). If nothing changed, the `&` line
is omitted too.

## Dirty-index check

- Staged-only changes (worktree == index ≠ HEAD): refresh proceeds, no warning.
- Unstaged-only changes: proceeds.
- Staged **and** unstaged changes present (any files, even different files):
  ```
  error: the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`
  ```
  stderr, exit 2, no output on stdout, no side effects. `-F/--force` or `-i/--index`
  override. Untracked files don't count as changes and are never refreshed.

## `--index` / `--update` / pathspecs

- `--index`: patch top set to index contents; unstaged worktree changes preserved.
- `-u/--update`: only files already in the target patch are refreshed; other staged
  files stay staged. (Dirty-index check still applies.)
- Pathspecs are relative to **cwd**; only matching files are refreshed, the rest stay
  staged/unstaged. Pathspec matching nothing → success (exit 0), output without `&`.
- Running from a subdirectory with **no** pathspec refreshes everything (cwd does not
  limit scope).
- Deletions (staged `git rm` or unstaged `rm`) are refreshed like other changes.

## Errors (stderr, exit codes)

| Case | Message | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| No applied patches (default target) | `error: no patches applied` | 2 |
| `-p` nonexistent | ``error: patch `nosuch` does not exist`` | 2 |
| `-p` hidden patch | ``error: hidden patch `p2` is not allowed`` | 2 |
| Detached HEAD | `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` | 2 |
| `-p branch:name` syntax | `error: invalid value 'other:op' for '--patch <patch>': invalid patch locator ` + backtick-quoted `other:op` + `\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--authdate` | `error: invalid value 'garbage' for '--authdate <date>': invalid date `garbage`` + blank + `For more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--author` | `error: invalid value 'NoEmail' for '--author <name-and-email>': invalid name and email `NoEmail`` + help line | 1 |
| `-m` twice | `error: the argument '--message <message>' cannot be used multiple times` + `\n\nUsage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| `-m ""` | `error: a value is required for '--message <message>' but none was supplied` + help line | 1 |
| Merge conflict (allow) | `error: merge conflicts; resolve conflicts manually then refresh or undo the operation with `stg undo --hard`.` | 3 |
| `--conflicts=disallow` | ``error: pushing patch `refresh-temp` would result in conflicts and push conflicts are disallowed`` | 3 |
| commit-msg hook fails | `<hook stderr>` then ``error: `commit-msg` hook returned 1`` | 2 |
| Empty message from editor | `error: aborting due to empty patch description` | 2 |
| Editor fails to run | `error: running editor: vi: No such file or directory (os error 2)` (falls back to `vi` when no EDITOR) | 2 |

## Conflict behavior (`refresh -p p1` conflicting with p2 above)

stdout:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp (conflict)
UU c.txt
```
stderr: `error: merge conflicts; ...` (above), exit 3.
State: temp patch left **applied and topmost**, patches above target unapplied
(`+ p1`, `> refresh-temp`, `- p2`); stack-log entry `refresh  (CONFLICT)`.
Conflict markers: `<<<<<<< current` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> patched`.
Resolution flow: fix files, `git add`, plain `stg refresh` (refreshes the temp patch,
new temp named `refresh-temp-1`), then `stg squash`/`stg push` etc.

With `--conflicts=disallow` (or `stgit.push.allow-conflicts=false`): stdout stops at
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
```
exit 3, temp patch left **unapplied** in the stack, target topmost applied.

On aborts (hook failure, empty editor message, editor spawn failure): only
`> refresh-temp (new)` is printed and the temp patch remains applied/topmost.

## Commit rewriting semantics

- Plain refresh preserves author name/email/date of the original patch commit;
  committer = current user, committer date = now.
- `--author "N <e>"`, `--authname`, `--authemail`, `--authdate` (accepts e.g.
  `2001-02-03T04:05:06`, `1999-12-31 23:59:59`, `now`) override the corresponding
  author fields; unspecified fields keep previous values.
- `--committer-date-is-author-date`: committer timestamp = author timestamp.
- `-m/--message`, `-f/--file` (`-` = stdin), `-e/--edit` replace the patch message.
  `-m` with no content changes still rewrites the commit (`&` shown).
- Trailers: `-s/--signoff`, `--ack`, `--review` default to committer identity; custom
  values require `=` syntax (`--signoff="Custom Signer <cs@x.com>"`) — a space-separated
  value is treated as a pathspec positional. Appended to existing trailers; exact
  duplicate trailers are suppressed (repeat `-s -s` adds one).
- `stgit.autosign` config: no effect observed on refresh.
- Resulting patch may become empty — allowed, kept in stack.

## Editor (`-e`)

- `hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...` printed to **stderr**.
- Editor template:
  ```
  Patch:  p1
  Author: Test <t@t.com>
  Date:   2026-08-07 12:17:06 +0000

  <current message>

  # Please enter the message for your patch. Lines starting with
  # '#' will be ignored. An empty message aborts the new patch.
  # The patch name and author information may also be modified.
  # The diff below is for reference. Any edits will be ignored.
  # ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
  # Do not modify or remove the line above.
  <diff, only with -d>
  ```
- Editing the `Patch:` header renames the patch: output gains `p1 => renamed` after
  the `& p1` line and ends `> renamed`.
- Editing `Author:` header changes the author.
- `-d` appends the **full patch diff** (40-char blob hashes) after the `>8` cut line;
  `-d` without `-e` is silently ignored.
- `-m` + `-e`: editor starts from the `-m` message.
- Empty resulting message → abort (exit 2, temp patch left).
